ladder.title: Percy Jackson and the Lightning Thief
ladder.author: Rick Riordan
ladder.note: Where it all began: the gods are real, and they live in America now.

ladder.title: Percy Jackson and the Sea of Monsters
ladder.author: Rick Riordan
ladder.note: The Odyssey’s monsters, retold at speed: spot the Sirens and the Cyclops.

ladder.title: The Lost Hero
ladder.author: Rick Riordan
ladder.note: Heroes of Olympus, book one: Greek and Roman gods collide.

ladder.title: The Hidden Oracle
ladder.author: Rick Riordan
ladder.note: The Trials of Apollo, book one: the god of poetry, stuck as a teenager.

ladder.title: Holes
ladder.author: Louis Sachar
ladder.note: A curse, a desert camp and a plot that clicks together perfectly.

ladder.title: Wonder
ladder.author: R. J. Palacio
ladder.note: Told from several points of view: a lesson in narrative voice.

ladder.title: Black Ships Before Troy
ladder.author: Rosemary Sutcliff
ladder.note: The Iliad retold in glorious prose: Hector, Achilles and the wooden horse.

ladder.title: The Wanderings of Odysseus
ladder.author: Rosemary Sutcliff
ladder.note: The Odyssey retold: the Cyclops, Circe, the Sirens and the long road home.

ladder.title: Northern Lights
ladder.author: Philip Pullman
ladder.note: Daemons, armoured bears and a girl who can read the truth.

ladder.title: Skellig
ladder.author: David Almond
ladder.note: Something strange in the garage. Short, haunting and beautifully written.

ladder.title: Wolf Brother
ladder.author: Michelle Paver
ladder.note: Six thousand years ago, a boy and a wolf cub against a demon bear.

ladder.title: Goodnight Mister Tom
ladder.author: Michelle Magorian
ladder.note: An evacuee in the Second World War. Moving, and sometimes hard to read.

ladder.title: The Hobbit
ladder.author: J. R. R. Tolkien
ladder.note: The original quest: riddles in the dark and a dragon on a hoard of gold.

ladder.title: Mythos
ladder.author: Stephen Fry
ladder.note: The Greek myths from the beginning, told with wit. Some grown-up humour.

ladder.title: A Wizard of Earthsea
ladder.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
ladder.note: A proud young wizard unleashes a shadow. Spare, wise and magical.

ladder.title: Treasure Island
ladder.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
ladder.note: Pirates, a map and Long John Silver, one of fiction’s great villains.

ladder.title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
ladder.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
ladder.note: Holmes and Watson on the moor. She has read the first chapter in English.

ladder.title: Animal Farm
ladder.author: George Orwell
ladder.note: A fable about power. Short, sharp and unforgettable.

ladder.title: Frankenstein
ladder.author: Mary Shelley
ladder.note: Written when she was a teenager. The creature is not the monster you expect.

ladder.title: Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde
ladder.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
ladder.note: A short, gripping gothic mystery, and a GCSE favourite.

ladder.title: A Christmas Carol
ladder.author: Charles Dickens
ladder.note: Four ghosts in one night. The perfect first Dickens.

ladder.title: Pride and Prejudice
ladder.author: Jane Austen
ladder.note: The funniest classic: start with the first chapter, which she has already met.

ladder.title: Jane Eyre
ladder.author: Charlotte Brontë
ladder.note: An orphan who refuses to be crushed, and a secret in the attic.

ladder.title: The Book Thief
ladder.author: Markus Zusak
ladder.note: Nazi Germany, narrated by Death. Powerful; best read with someone to talk to.

ladder.title: The Odyssey (translated by Emily Wilson)
ladder.author: Homer
ladder.note: The real thing, in a clear, fast modern verse translation.

ladder.title: Oedipus the King
ladder.author: Sophocles
ladder.note: The greatest Greek tragedy: a detective story where the detective is the culprit.

ladder.title: The King Must Die
ladder.author: Mary Renault
ladder.note: Theseus, the labyrinth and the bull-leapers of Crete, told as if it really happened.

ladder.title: Medusa
ladder.author: Jessie Burton
ladder.note: The Gorgon tells her own story: a beautifully illustrated retelling for teenage readers.

ladder.title: Percy Jackson’s Greek Gods
ladder.author: Rick Riordan
ladder.note: The Olympians’ own stories, told with Percy’s jokes: a great companion to her Greek.

ladder.title: The Odyssey
ladder.author: Gillian Cross
ladder.note: A gripping retelling of the whole journey home, with striking illustrations by Neil Packer.
